definition: Findings definitions for healthy weight gain

findings.title: Not Eating Frequently Enough
findings.clinicalExplanation: Your current meal frequency may not provide enough calories throughout the day to support healthy weight gain.
findings.userExplanation: Eating only a few times each day makes it difficult to consistently consume the energy your body needs to gain weight.

findings.title: Protein Intake Needs Improvement
findings.clinicalExplanation: Your meals may not consistently provide enough protein to effectively support muscle repair and growth.
findings.userExplanation: Your meals consistently lack enough protein to effectively support muscle growth and repair.

findings.title: Missing Extra Calorie Opportunities
findings.clinicalExplanation: Healthy snacks between meals are an effective way to increase daily calorie intake without relying on large meals.
findings.userExplanation: You are missing out on extra calories between meals, making healthy weight gain much harder.

findings.title: Not Using Liquid Nutrition
findings.clinicalExplanation: Liquid calories are an efficient strategy for increasing energy intake, especially when appetite is limited.
findings.userExplanation: You are not utilizing liquid calories, which is a missed opportunity to easily increase your daily energy intake.

findings.title: Low Appetite Is Limiting Progress
findings.clinicalExplanation: Reduced appetite makes it difficult to consume enough calories consistently.
findings.userExplanation: Even the best weight gain plan won't work if eating enough feels difficult every day.

findings.title: You Feel Full Too Quickly
findings.clinicalExplanation: Feeling full early during meals limits total calorie intake and slows healthy weight gain.
findings.userExplanation: Feeling full too quickly makes it very difficult for you to eat the larger portions needed to gain weight.

findings.title: Limited Muscle Building Stimulus
findings.clinicalExplanation: Without regular resistance training, much of the additional weight gained may come from body fat rather than lean muscle.
findings.userExplanation: Without regular strength training, the extra calories you consume are more likely to be stored as fat rather than built into muscle.

findings.title: Workouts May Have Stalled
findings.clinicalExplanation: Muscles adapt over time. Without gradually increasing training intensity, muscle growth slows.
findings.userExplanation: Your workouts lack progression, meaning your muscles don't have a reason to continue growing.

findings.title: High Cardio May Slow Weight Gain
findings.clinicalExplanation: Large amounts of cardio increase calorie expenditure and make maintaining a calorie surplus more difficult.
findings.userExplanation: You may be burning many of the extra calories you're trying to consume.

findings.title: Your Lifestyle Burns A Lot Of Calories
findings.clinicalExplanation: A physically demanding lifestyle increases daily calorie needs beyond average estimates.
findings.userExplanation: Because you're active throughout the day, you may need substantially more food than you realize.

findings.title: Sleep May Be Limiting Muscle Growth
findings.clinicalExplanation: Inadequate sleep reduces recovery quality and may slow muscle development.
findings.userExplanation: Your body builds and repairs muscle most effectively during quality sleep.

findings.title: Stress Could Affect Your Progress
findings.clinicalExplanation: High stress can reduce appetite, interfere with recovery, and make healthy habits harder to maintain.
findings.userExplanation: Managing stress can make it easier to eat consistently and recover from training.

findings.title: Your Recovery Needs Improvement
findings.clinicalExplanation: Poor recovery reduces your body's ability to adapt and grow after exercise.
findings.userExplanation: Recovery is where muscle growth actually happens—not during the workout itself.

findings.title: Your Body May Need More Rest
findings.clinicalExplanation: Too little recovery between training sessions may reduce long-term progress.
findings.userExplanation: Regular rest days help your muscles rebuild and become stronger.

findings.title: You've Always Struggled To Gain Weight
findings.clinicalExplanation: Your history suggests long-term difficulty gaining weight, which often requires a more structured nutrition strategy.
findings.userExplanation: Your body may naturally require more planning and consistency than others to gain healthy weight.

findings.title: Previous Attempts Haven't Worked
findings.clinicalExplanation: Repeated unsuccessful attempts suggest that previous strategies may not have addressed the real barriers.
findings.userExplanation: The right plan isn't just eating more—it's improving the habits that matter most.

findings.title: Skipping Meals Is Holding You Back
findings.clinicalExplanation: Missing meals reduces total daily calorie intake and makes healthy weight gain much harder.
findings.userExplanation: Every missed meal is a missed opportunity to fuel healthy growth.

findings.title: Larger Meals Feel Difficult
findings.clinicalExplanation: Difficulty eating larger portions limits your ability to consistently consume enough calories.
findings.userExplanation: You experience discomfort when trying to eat larger portions, heavily limiting your calorie intake.

findings.title: Fear Of Fat Gain Is Affecting Your Progress
findings.clinicalExplanation: Avoiding adequate food intake because of concerns about body fat can unintentionally prevent healthy muscle gain.
findings.userExplanation: A balanced nutrition plan helps you build lean muscle while minimizing unnecessary fat gain.

findings.title: Your Confidence Needs Building
findings.clinicalExplanation: Low confidence can reduce consistency and make it harder to stay committed.
findings.userExplanation: Believing you can succeed is an important part of long-term progress.

findings.title: Consistency May Be Your Biggest Challenge
findings.clinicalExplanation: Without strong commitment, even the best nutrition and training plans become difficult to follow.
findings.userExplanation: Small habits practiced consistently produce far better results than perfect plans followed briefly.

findings.title: Your Appetite Supports Healthy Weight Gain
findings.clinicalExplanation: A healthy appetite makes it easier to consistently consume enough calories.
findings.userExplanation: This is one of your biggest strengths and will make progress easier.

findings.title: You're Prioritizing Protein Well
findings.clinicalExplanation: Consistent protein intake provides the building blocks needed for muscle growth.
findings.userExplanation: Keep including quality protein in every meal to support healthy weight gain.

findings.title: Your Training Supports Muscle Growth
findings.clinicalExplanation: Regular resistance training provides the necessary stimulus for lean muscle development.
findings.userExplanation: You're giving your body a strong reason to build muscle instead of simply gaining fat.

findings.title: Your Recovery Habits Are Strong
findings.clinicalExplanation: Good sleep and recovery create an excellent environment for muscle growth.
findings.userExplanation: Recovery is one of your strengths—keep protecting it.

findings.title: You're Ready To Succeed
findings.clinicalExplanation: High commitment significantly increases the likelihood of achieving long-term healthy weight gain.
findings.userExplanation: Your willingness to stay consistent gives you an excellent foundation for success.

findings.title: Chronic Calorie Deficit
findings.clinicalExplanation: The user consistently struggles to consume enough calories due to low meal frequency, reduced appetite, and feeling full too quickly.
findings.userExplanation: You consistently struggle to consume enough calories due to low meal frequency, reduced appetite, and feeling full too quickly.

findings.title: Poor Muscle Growth Strategy
findings.clinicalExplanation: Even if calorie intake improves, muscle gain will remain limited without adequate protein and resistance training.
findings.userExplanation: Even if your calorie intake improves, muscle gain will remain limited without adequate protein and resistance training.

findings.title: Hard Gainer Profile
findings.clinicalExplanation: The user naturally burns large amounts of energy while struggling to eat enough, making healthy weight gain particularly challenging.
findings.userExplanation: You naturally burn large amounts of energy while struggling to eat enough, making healthy weight gain particularly challenging.

findings.title: Recovery Limiting Progress
findings.clinicalExplanation: Recovery capacity is limiting muscle growth despite other healthy efforts.
findings.userExplanation: Your recovery capacity is limiting muscle growth despite other healthy efforts.

findings.title: Busy Lifestyle Barrier
findings.clinicalExplanation: A busy routine is preventing consistent calorie intake throughout the day.
findings.userExplanation: A busy routine is preventing consistent calorie intake throughout the day.

findings.title: Fear-Based Under Eating
findings.clinicalExplanation: Psychological concerns about gaining body fat are preventing adequate calorie intake.
findings.userExplanation: Concerns about gaining body fat are preventing you from adequately eating enough calories.

findings.title: High Calorie Burn
findings.clinicalExplanation: Daily calorie expenditure is extremely high, making it difficult to maintain a calorie surplus.
findings.userExplanation: Your daily calorie expenditure is extremely high, making it difficult to maintain a calorie surplus.

findings.title: Strong Lean Gain Foundation
findings.clinicalExplanation: The user already has the core habits needed to gain lean muscle effectively.
findings.userExplanation: You already have the core habits needed to gain lean muscle effectively.

findings.title: Highly Committed Learner
findings.clinicalExplanation: The user demonstrates excellent readiness for long-term behaviour change.
findings.userExplanation: You demonstrate excellent readiness for long-term behaviour change.

findings.title: Complete Healthy Weight Gain Lifestyle
findings.clinicalExplanation: The user consistently follows the key nutritional, training, recovery, and behavioural habits associated with successful healthy weight gain.
findings.userExplanation: You consistently follow the key nutritional, training, recovery, and behavioural habits associated with successful healthy weight gain.
